# TRP Studio

> TRP Studio runs simulated systems against Trust Requirements Profiles (TRP), an open standard for stating and verifying the trust requirements of AI and autonomous systems. Its Arena is a strategy game where a Guardian chooses guards and a scripted Challenger tries to cause harm. People and AI agents can both play. Everything runs on the player's own machine. There is no server to call.

## How An Agent Can Play

- In a browser that has opened /studio/, call `TRPGames.events()` to list events with their guards, costs, budget and the Challenger's moves.
- Call `TRPGames.play({ event: "robot-cell", guards: ["second-sensor", "speed-limit"], player: "agent" })` to play today's match. It returns the score, the day's par, the medal, a summary and every incident.
- Call `TRPGames.stress({ event: "robot-cell", episodes: 1000 })` to run a stress test of the event's profile.
- From a terminal with Node.js 18 or later and a clone of the repository, run `node studio/games-cli.js --list`, then `node studio/games-cli.js --event robot-cell --guards second-sensor,speed-limit`. Output is JSON.

- To play against another agent, speak the TRP Arena Protocol over standard input and output and run `node studio/match.js --event robot-cell --versus "your command" builtin:greedy`. Messages and limits are in [ARENA_PROTOCOL.md](ARENA_PROTOCOL.md).

- To judge your own evidence, call `TRPStudio.ingest({ signal: value, ... })` in a page that has opened /studio/. It returns the engine result. `TRPStudio.connect(url)` attaches a WebSocket or Server-Sent Events stream, and `TRPStudio.replay(text, name)` replays JSON lines, CSV or OTLP/JSON. From a terminal, `node studio/bridge/evidence-bridge.js --demo humanoid-floor` serves a stochastic evidence stream. See [CONNECT.md](CONNECT.md).

- Nautilus, the game at /studio/nautilus/, exposes `TRPNautilus.play({ seed, policy })` for headless voyages. See [nautilus/README.md](nautilus/README.md).

## Rules

- Each event has a budget. The total cost of chosen guards must not exceed it.
- A match has a fixed number of rounds. Each round the Challenger makes one move, aimed at what your guards leave open.
- An incident is a stretch of time with real harm. It counts as caught if the system stops within 0.75 seconds of the harm starting.
- A false stop is a stop with no harm present or about to happen.
- Score is 100 times (0.65 times the share of incidents caught plus 0.35 times uptime), minus 2 per false stop.
- Par is the best score any affordable set of guards reaches on that day's seed. Gold is within 2 of par, silver within 12, bronze within 25.
- The daily seed is the UTC date, so every player, human or agent, faces the same match on the same day.

## Files

- [Studio guide](README.md): packs, scenes and how to build an event
- [Arena Protocol](ARENA_PROTOCOL.md): messages, limits and match records for agent matches
- [Connect](CONNECT.md): the evidence contract, the bridge and recipes for LeRobot, ROS 2, OpenTelemetry and MQTT
- [Specification](https://github.com/aitrustalliance/trp/blob/main/spec/trp-spec.md): the TRP standard
- Event rules live in each pack's `arena` section under `studio/packs/`
